operations.comment: ; Bank 0 exposes three fixed jump slots: initialize, submit request (A), and tick.
; These CPU aliases require physical PRG bank 0 in the $8000 slot.
; Fourth bank-zero API slot enters a blocking DAC playback loop; unlike the tick API, it does not preserve frame timing.
; Four low pointer bytes followed by four high bytes select per-channel software repeat stacks. AdvanceOverlayStream loads these into sound_loop_stack_lo/hi; the pointed storage is RAM, not ROM.
; Initialize the four non-DMC sound channels and clear the $0600 page.
; Each channel gets the same initial period-table pointer ($805F), sweep and
; control defaults. Request slots and fractional clock start empty; clock step
; starts at $FFFF. X/Y and A are clobbered.
; 96 little-endian hardware period words for pitched channels. Initialization selects CPU $805F; note indexing reads each low/high pair. This array describes periods, not PCM sample bytes.
; Submit A as a sound identifier. Zero clears both pending requests.
; The header pointer table at $8AFE uses two bytes per identifier. A header
; with bit 7 clear replaces the primary request; bit 7 set selects an overlay.
; Compatibility masks can reject an overlay against either currently queued sound.
; Identifiers and the exact conflict-table extent remain unresolved.
; After loading the current request header, reject an incompatible replacement; otherwise fall through to queue the new request.
; Strip the loaded marker from A and select the corresponding comparison header
; in the same two-byte pointer table. The caller retains Y for header access.
; Check the bit for request (A originally saved in sound_request_scratch) in
; the comparison header's indirect compatibility bitset. Request minus one chooses
; byte index and bit index; the scratch identifier is restored before return.
; A=0 rejects the request when this test is reached; a set bit permits it.
; The eight compatibility masks are classified at SoundChannelBitMasks.
; Eight one-bit masks serve the request compatibility bitset. The suffix beginning CPU $81B3 also selects the four channel-ownership bits. These are CPU aliases in physical PRG bank 0.
; One sound tick: accept changed requests, advance the fractional clock, then
; walk four channels in descending order. Primary countdowns advance on clock
; carry; overlay countdowns advance every call. An overlay owns its channel
; while active, suppressing the primary register write without discarding the
; primary stream position. The flag and envelope helpers live later in bank 0.
; Flag bit 4 marks this primary note boundary in the shared scratch byte.
; Clear the note-end and overlay-ownership bits, interpret the next primary
; stream item, and reload this channel's delay.
; An empty overlay channel mask clears its request and loaded latches,
; then joins the primary retrigger check. Active masks continue into ownership testing.
; An active overlay marks ownership before its per-call delay is decremented.
; Without an overlay, a primary channel may rewrite its period at a fresh
; countdown value. Otherwise only the envelope/control update is needed.
; Finish the current channel envelope, clear per-tick scratch and scan
; backward through the remaining channels; a negative index ends the sound tick.
; Add the 16-bit clock step plus one to the fractional accumulator. Carry
; produces a primary tick unless sound_clock_hold is nonzero. This is a
; fractional-rate scheduler; no musical tempo unit is assumed.
; Choose full period/control output, control-only output, or silence according
; to primary flags, overlay ownership, and the shared note-boundary scratch.
; Channel 2 additionally resets the triangle linear counter after period output.
; Reload each nonzero request when it differs from its last loaded marker.
; Primary and overlay requests have separate ownership masks and streams.
; Release old primary channels that are not protected by an overlay. Mark
; the request loaded with bit 7, read its header channel mask, then consume
; low/high stream pointer pairs for selected channels in descending order.
; Reset note, transpose, envelope and countdown state for each loaded channel.
; The three-byte header prefix is skipped before the per-channel pointer pairs.
; Overlay identifiers $19/$1A hold/resume the primary fractional clock.
; Release previous overlay channels, mark the new request loaded, then read
; its channel mask and pointer pairs after the three-byte header prefix.
; Reset overlay parser state and delays; pulse channels receive parameter 2.
; The later comparison against channel 2 follows a branch excluding that value;
; it is preserved exactly, without assigning it an intended triangle behavior.
; Reset control for every channel in the previous overlay mask before loading
; a replacement. Preserve the selected index for helpers that repurpose X.
; Interpret primary stream commands until a note ($80..$8F) is found. Bytes
; below $80 replace the delay reload; bytes $90 and above dispatch commands.
; Commit consumed bytes back to the channel pointer after interpretation.
; Stream commands may deliberately unwind the parser rather than return here.
; A note stores its low four bits as the period-table index. Reset volume
; from the envelope step, then initialize envelope timing from flag bits
; $40/$20/$10. These modes are mechanical names; exact instrument meanings
; and valid flag combinations remain unresolved.
; Shared return after setting the initial envelope accumulator.
; Store the computed duration as the envelope limit before the existing accumulator initialization continues.
; Clear this channel envelope accumulator and return.
; Compute (delay reload >> 2) times the envelope flag low nibble, modulo 256.
; Zero nibble executes 256 additions because the decrement follows the add.
; Restore X from sound_channel_index; return the duration in A.
; Advance the 16-bit stream base by Y consumed bytes; Y is left unchanged.
; Commands that redirect the stream reset Y themselves to avoid double advance.
; Load overlay stream and its per-channel repeat-stack backing pointer from
; $800C/$8010, execute commands until a byte below $90 sets the delay, then
; commit consumption. The low/high pointer bytes are the classified SoundStackPointerBytes.
; Unknown; physical 1222..1223
; Single zero after a tail jump and before a separate sound entry. Stored
; zero versus an unentered BRK fragment remains unresolved; sample bounds
; and no observed execution do not discriminate code from data.
; Overlay commands update shared control and period state before output.
; X+4 selects the overlay control arrays, whose base symbols describe the
; primary four entries. WriteChannelControl restores the physical channel X
; from sound_channel_index before the period helper is called.
; Write overlay period low every update. Flag $40 permits a high-period
; write, which reloads the hardware length counter; channel 3 uses the noise
; period/length registers instead. High pitched-channel period is masked to
; four bits after forcing bit 3.
; X&3 selects pulse, triangle or noise hardware; X>=4 selects overlay state.
; Pulse duty comes from low duty bits or the alternate lookup when flag $80
; is set. Overlay delay bit 7 clears constant-volume mode. Combine volume
; and mode bits, map channel to the four-register APU stride, then restore X.
; Triangle only receives a control write when the selected volume is zero.

; Alternating pulse-control bits $00,$40,$00,$40, read by SelectAlternatePulseDuty before its upper-bit mask. The preceding unconditional branch skips these bytes; the old BRK fallthrough was invalid. The complete selector domain remains unresolved.
; For pitched channels, index a two-byte period table with twice
; (transpose + note), add the signed byte period adjustment, and write the
; period registers. Channel 3 writes the noise index directly. X is temporarily
; multiplied by four for register selection and restored on the ordinary path.
; The sweep guard compares this multiplied X with 2, so it never excludes
; channel 2 for ordinary channel indices 0..3; preserve that exact behavior.
; The negative-adjustment path uses SBC for the high byte after the low ADC.
; It is retained literally; do not assume a conventional signed 16-bit sum.
; Restore the saved logical channel index in A; this small alternate return leaves X unchanged.
; Write the note low nibble as noise period, then reload noise length
; with$08. X selects the channel note; no pulse-period table is consulted.
; Overlay-ownership flag $20 suppresses primary envelope writes. With envelope
; flag $40 and nonzero volume, either count down to silence or add the step
; to an accumulator, subtracting the limit and decrementing volume for each
; crossing. Pulse duty countdown and optional period refresh follow. Valid
; nonzero envelope limits are a stream-format assumption, not checked here.
; Decrement the duty countdown. The continuation reloads it and advances duty
; only when the countdown expires.
; A zero duty countdown reloads its period and advances the duty selector; other ticks retain the selector.
; Tail-call the shared channel-control writer after envelope/period work.
; A is command byte minus $90. Fetch its two-byte CPU target from $8646,
; restore channel X and jump indirectly. SoundCommandTargetWords contains 51
; target words; stream validity must keep the command index inside that domain.

; 51 little-endian CPU handler targets consumed by DispatchSoundCommand after subtracting $90 and doubling the command byte. All targets require physical bank 0 at $8000. Several handlers intentionally discard parser return frames; this is not an ordinary-call table.
; Set channel flag $20, discard one return address, and return out of the
; current parser call. This is a nonlocal parser exit, not an ordinary helper.
; Raise the stored transpose by twelve semitone indices, wrapping at 256.
; Lower the stored transpose by twelve semitone indices, wrapping at 256.
; Consume one stream byte as the new transpose index.
; Consume one byte as the envelope step and initial note volume parameter.
; Set channel flags $10 and $20. The tick path tests these flags at note
; boundaries and suppresses further primary envelope writes while $20 is set.
; Consume one byte as pulse duty/control selection.
; Consume a countdown period and enable primary duty cycling. The reload and current countdown start together.
; Disable duty cycling and restore duty selector two; envelope and note state are retained.
; Select envelope flag $40 while clearing $30; share the ramp command limit-byte consumer.
; Select envelope bits $60, clear $10, and consume the accumulator limit.
; This chooses repeated volume reductions as the accumulator crosses a limit.
; Set envelope bits $50 and clear $20 before merging the next stream byte.
; This chooses countdown-to-silence mode; the low nibble scales duration.
; Alternate entry forces all envelope mode bits $70 before merging a byte.
; No caller or intended instrument role is asserted for this entry.
; Clear the three envelope mode bits, retaining the low parameter nibble and flag $80.
; Consume the stored sweep parameter. Its exact later modulation role is unresolved.
; Enable the primary period-refresh flag and initialize two per-channel counters from one byte. The counters have no classified consumer here; no vibrato meaning is assumed.
; Clear primary period refresh without discarding the note or period-table state.
; Replace the stream cursor with a little-endian target. Y resets to zero; no return frame is saved.
; Remove this channel from the primary mask. If no overlay owns it, reset
; hardware control; then discard the dispatcher return address so the stream
; parser exits. The primary and overlay stream positions remain separate.
; Push a repeat frame into the channel's indirect stack: high return byte,
; low return byte, count. Cursor advances past the count before saving, and Y
; restarts at zero. No stack-capacity check is made here.
; Decrement the top repeat count. While nonzero, restore its stream position;
; at zero remove the three-byte frame and restore the caller's consumed-byte Y.
; An initial zero repeat count therefore wraps and repeats 256 times.
; Equivalent stream jump entry used by a separate command-table slot. The pointer names describe shared parser storage.
; Consume an overlay delay, discard the command-dispatch return address and leave the parser so its caller commits this cursor.
; Consume one byte into the shared stream parameter; its full use is unresolved.
; Read low/high overlay period bytes and mark flag $40 so output rewrites
; the hardware high-period register and length counter.
; Consume the per-channel pulse parameter. Later consumers are not fully
; classified, so this name describes the storage role only.
; Consume one byte into this channel's sweep-register slot, then restore logical X. The command format must choose a meaningful hardware channel.
; Add an unsigned byte to the channel stream parameter, wrapping at 256.
; Add one unsigned stream byte to the overlay period. Carry updates the high
; byte and sets rewrite flag $40. Without carry the high-write flag is retained.
; Increment the stored stream parameter, wrapping at 256.
; Add a little-endian word to the overlay period and request a high-register rewrite. INY preserves carry between the byte additions.
; Increment the per-channel pulse parameter with byte wraparound.
; Subtract one stream byte from the stored channel parameter, wrapping at 256.
; Subtract one unsigned stream byte from overlay period, propagating borrow
; to the high byte. A borrow also sets the high-period rewrite flag; without
; borrow the existing flag is retained.
; The completed borrow path requests a high-period/length write before the shared return.
; Decrement the channel parameter with byte wraparound.
; Subtract a little-endian stream word from the overlay period, propagating borrow, and request a high-register rewrite.
; Shift the stored 16-bit overlay period left once; overflow is discarded.
; Shift the unsigned overlay period right once. These shift commands retain the current rewrite flag.
; Remove the overlay channel bit and discard three return addresses before
; falling into channel-control reset. This terminates the nested overlay parse
; and output path rather than returning to the command loop.
; Reset pulse/noise control and sweep or triangle linear control, then restore
; the primary period for the channel. This restores primary hardware state when
; overlay ownership ends; it does not clear all primary stream state.
; Set overlay flag $80. The classified output path does not establish its game or instrument meaning.
; Clear overlay flag $80 while preserving the other overlay flags.

; Consume a literal hardware-register frame and delay. Triangle omits the sweep write but still consumes that byte. Discard three return addresses and resume cursor commitment in the outer overlay caller.
; Write period low/high, consume the next delay byte, then bypass the nested overlay output path.
; Consume a little-endian period-table pointer for this channel. Target banking and table extent are stream-format obligations.
; Consume a little-endian 16-bit fractional clock step. The primary clock
; adds this value plus one each tick; overlay countdowns use the call rate.
; Begin the single-level repeat form: consume its byte count, advance the
; stream cursor and save the loop start in per-channel low/high arrays.
; This storage is distinct from the three-byte nested-repeat stack.
; Decrement the single-level count; nonzero restores the saved stream start
; with Y=0. Zero continues after the repeat command. Initial zero wraps.
; Call a stream subroutine: consume a little-endian target, save the cursor
; after those two bytes in per-channel return arrays, then switch the stream
; base to the target with Y=0. This return storage supports one active call.
; Restore the stream subroutine return pointer and restart consumption at Y=0.
; Consume a new primary request, discard three return addresses, and leave the nested parser/update path. The next sound tick observes the request.
; Consume the per-channel period adjustment used by the existing note-period calculation.
; Consume the byte at the sound-state base. No classified consumer establishes a more specific control meaning.

; Stream CPU $A700..$B100, end exclusive, into the 7-bit DAC after shifting each source byte right. This blocking routine requires the matching bank-one sample view at $A000; it does not map that bank itself.
; Y stays zero while the zero-page pointer advances through ten pages. The fixed delay controls sample cadence; interrupts can lengthen it.
; Delay 84 loop iterations between sample writes; X is scratch.
; Bounded uniform $FF byte run; adjacent bytes and code conflicts were
; inspected in analysis/uniform-data-boundaries.json. Non-code classification
; is retained; no consumer, padding intent, or sample format is established.

; Sound request pointers, headers and command streams share this region and continue in bank 1. Existing pointer/command consumers and repeated stream forms establish non-code; exact individual stream boundaries and request semantics remain unresolved. Keep the region whole rather than inventing a complete stream grammar.

; Continuation of the sound request/header/command-stream region in physical bank 1. Bank-zero parsers read it through CPU $A000..$A6FF when bank 1 occupies $A000. Internal stream/header subdivisions remain unresolved after consumer and repeated-format inspection.

; Physical PRG bank 5 in the $8000 CPU slot. Mask $02C1 to six bits and
; subtract 7 to select parallel parameter tables, spaced seven bytes apart.
; Copy nine table bytes into initialization state; $9A02 feeds both $69 and
; $0202. Set fixed parameters $8C=$A9 and $89=4; stage values >=8 also set
; $0261=$FF. No index bound is checked, so valid selector range is an entry
; precondition. Extended-stage parameter arrays are classified; precise game meanings
; of the remaining destination fields are unresolved.
; Nine parallel arrays with seven bytes each. The extended-stage initializer uses the
; selected stage as the within-array index; these are field arrays rather than nine seven-
; byte object records. Exact game meanings follow the corresponding destination stores.
; Load fifteen parallel parameter fields for screen_override minus one. The caller must
; supply1..9 and physical bank5 at CPU$8000; this unchecked initializer does not validate the
; index. Fields configure stage phase, scroll pages, tile-stream position and timers for
; the selected screen. Set the remaining setup byte to $60.
; Fifteen parallel arrays with nine bytes each. The screen-override initializer selects
; one of nine variants and copies one byte per destination field. Keep field roles tied to
; destination stores; natural selector reachability is separate.
; Initialize the Factory scene called from bank7. Clear scroll position, world
; coordinates, transition counters and override; select page4, column19 and the literal
; layer-page/timer defaults. This is a setup contract, not proof that a natural boss
; completion reaches it. Both physical banks5/7 must remain mapped in their respective
; lower slots.
; Eleven repeated $01/$FF parameter-like bytes between an accepted return and a separate call-like
; fragment. The surrounding fragment and references do not recover a specific consumer or schema.
; B5NormalizeAnimationType
; Check the native camera helper. When its result is nonzero, enter the alternate
; subtract/copy helper with X=5, then clear type bit7 in the selected slot.
; C607 subtracts RAM $60,X before copying44 player bytes; it is not a type initializer.
; B5PrepareMotionStateThree
; Unless low7 direction bits already equal3, call the native OAM/bound-copy
; alternates and test phase probe>=2. Install state3, frame4, countdown0 and
